title: Her son and aunt urge her to join the March of Dimes show
summary: Her small son and aunt Augusta urged her to appear at the Hollywood High School March of Dimes show, as Betty Hall Jones had.

blocks.x: It was a huge -- oh, it was a tremendous thing. It was just like the telethons are today. Thank God they don't need that now. But at that time, this telethon was -- show, rather, was going to be at the Hollywood High School, and he says, 'Momma, why don't you appear on that show.' He says, 'All my little friends are going to be there,' because they

were talking about it at all the schools, you see. This was the way they had to do to make the money, because there was no such thing as telethons, today, where you can make hundreds of thousands of dollars at one pitch, you know. And he said, "Why don't you?" I says, "Well, I'm not known. These people that are going to appear on the show, like Betty Hutton and Bob Hope and many others," I said, "Well, they're all people who are very well known, they're famous people," I said, "Momma's not famous." And he said, "But momma, you're just as good as they are. Momma, why can't you? I want my friends to hear you play and sing." He said, "You could play." And I said, "Well, you know, it isn't done that way." And so in the meantime it was sort of in the back of my mind, you know. I listened to what he was saying.

So my aunt, Augusta Glover, called me and she said, "Listen," she says, "I've been reading about this show that they're going to have at the Hollywood High School, the March of Dimes thing." She says, "Why aren't you -- why don't you get onto that." Well, I think my friend Betty Hall Jones, who is a very dear friend of mine, and a very marvelous, magnificent entertainer, pianist and entertainer, and Betty and I had been friends for years. When I first came here I also met her. So she says, "Why don't you get on that show." Like I think Betty had recorded. I know she had. She had recorded for some little label, and this little label, you know, were trying to

push her, you know. She was at that time boogie-woogie. Well, Betty comes from Kansas, and of course she had a great flair for boggie, you know, boogie-woogie. And of course she had gotten sort of into entertaining by this time. She had gotten away from, somewhat away from some of the boogie, but she was still, you know, using this thing.

So on this particular show this is what she did. So I -- my aunt said, "Well, why don't you --," and I said, "Well, Talmadge mentioned --," that's my son -- "Well, Talmadge mentioned the fact that he would like to hear me and see me on the show." Then I told her what I told him. And she says, "Well, why don't you call them and ask them. I think it would be wonderful if you could get on. If Betty can get on, you ought to be able to get on there too." I said, "But Betty has made records and I have not got a record reputation." I said, "When you have made records already, well the people have heard your records, so even if they're not hit records, you know."

They would be played. She said, "Well, people know you. You've played around here a long time." Because I'd get on a job, one job I was on -- I think I talked about that, where I was on that job for about two and a half years or so. So anyway, I did. I thought, I think I'll send a telegram.
